tools.name: list_cro_skills
tools.description: Find Postclick methods for prioritising page fixes, ad-to-page message match, buyer objections, copy edits and client test briefs. Returns starter requests and portable skill downloads. No account needed.

tools.name: run_cro_skill
tools.description: For page fixes, message match, buyer objections, copy rewrites or a client test brief. Finds an existing audit by page URL or client name and retrieves the selected skill plus its relevant evidence in one call. Returns source material for the requested deliverable, not a new AI analysis. Audit sugge

tools.name: check_balance
tools.description: Read what the connected Postclick account covers now: its credit balance and how many credits an audit or a build uses, or the pages left on a page plan. Use before starting an audit, design or build, and when the user asks what their account covers. A missing figure is unknown.

tools.name: audit_page
tools.description: Start a new landing-page audit when requested. Use check_balance for page coverage and follow the user's permission. First search for existing work when the request concerns a prior audit. Pass campaign context already supplied. Returns an audit_id; use get_audit with wait:25, then run_cro_skill for

tools.name: get_audit
tools.description: Read audit status, changed progress, server elapsed time and ranked findings with typed edits. Use wait:25 while running. A failed, cancelled or stalled run is not a finished report. Once complete, use run_cro_skill or ask_audit for the relevant buyer, copy or offer evidence. Reading does not author

tools.name: get_audit_report
tools.description: Read the complete stored audit as markdown for a full review. It can be long: use topic or ask_audit for one question, or run_cro_skill for a specific deliverable. Missing and withheld sections remain unknown. Buyer journeys are modelled, not customer research.

tools.name: get_competitors
tools.description: Costs nothing. Returns the competitor layer of a finished audit: the competitors bidding on the same clicks, the live ads Google is serving for each of them with the keyword, search volume and CPC behind every one, the landing pages those ads click to, which competitor advertises most, the advertise

tools.name: ask_audit
tools.description: Uses no credits. Answers one question from a completed audit by returning that part of it in full: small enough to give the user whole, unlike the entire report. For follow-up questions about a page that has an audit. Topics: `buyers` for who is on this page, what each one is afraid of, the exact wo

tools.name: generate_concepts
tools.description: Draws design directions for an existing audit as rendered pictures. Only when the user asks to see designs: build_page needs none and sets the look itself. Use check_balance for page coverage and follow the user's permission. Returns a run to resume with get_concepts.

tools.name: get_concepts
tools.description: Uses no credits. Returns every concept rendered for an audit, each with its image URLs and a link to view it full size, and a runs.active count of how many are still rendering. A pack takes 3 to 8 minutes. With wait (up to 300 seconds) the call holds open and returns when a design lands, the stage m

tools.name: build_page
tools.description: Builds a complete HTML landing page for an audit when the user asks and their plan covers it. No design is needed first: the designer sets the look and works the audit's fixes in. Set keep to improve the page they already have and keep its look. Pass concept_id only to build from a design the user s

tools.name: get_build
tools.description: Uses no credits. Returns the build's status and, once finished, the complete page. A build takes about 10 to 20 minutes. With wait (up to 300 seconds) the call holds open and returns when the stage moves or the page is ready. A status of running is non-terminal and contains no page. By default the H

tools.name: share_page
tools.description: Uses no credits. Mints a public no-login link that anyone can open, including someone with no account, for sending a page, design or audit to someone else. App and dashboard links need a login; this link does not. Pass build_run_id to share a finished built page. Pass concept_id to share a design; i

tools.name: export_page
tools.description: Uses no credits. Packages a finished page as a zip that runs on any static host: index.html with every image it uses pulled into assets/, plus a README and metadata.json. Returns a download link. share_page gives a link to look at instead. It also returns implementation_prompt: step by step instruct

tools.name: describe
tools.description: List what is in the account when the user asks to see their work. For a page fix, copy rewrite or designer brief, call run_cro_skill directly; no account overview is needed first.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Uses no credits. Finds anything in this workspace by words: a domain, a page URL, a client's name, a design's caption, a project. Returns an address for each hit that you pass straight to `fetch`. Use this the moment somebody refers to work they have already done — "the zoomdrain page", "last month'

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Uses no credits. Reads any single thing by its address, which looks like postclick://audit/<id> and comes from `search`, from `describe`, or from any other tool's answer. A plain id works too if that is all you have. `expand` is what makes this worth calling: pass `*` and you get everything attached

tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Uses no credits. Every design, page capture and logo has an asset_id on the field that holds it. Pass it here. Which form you ask for depends entirely on where the picture is going, and getting it wrong is expensive. `as: "url"` is the DEFAULT AND USUALLY RIGHT one: a public link, no login, full siz

tools.name: publish_page
tools.description: Uses no credits. Takes HTML you wrote and hosts it at postclick.ppc.io/r/<name>, public, no login, ready to send to a client. A client gets a plain web page, not a link into a chat. We do not template the page, style it or add anything to it: it is exactly the report you wrote. USE PLAIN IMAGE LINKS

tools.name: save_note
tools.description: Uses no credits. Attaches anything you like to any record: who the client is, what they were charged, which findings they have already fixed, when you last sent them a report. Any name, any value. We never look inside it and the audit engine never reads it, so it cannot change what Postclick does. I

tools.name: get_notes
tools.description: Uses no credits. Returns the notes saved against one record, or every note in the workspace when no address is given. Worth calling at the start of a repeat job, so a monthly report picks up whatever the last one left behind.

findings.detail: Tool "run_cro_skill" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: skill, latest, page, audit_id, section, context

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.ppc.io" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_cro_skills, run_cro_skill, get_audit_report, get_concepts, get_build, search, get_asset, publish_page · Private data: build_page, get_build, share_page, get_asset, publish_page, save_note, get_notes · Public sink: share_page, export_page, get_asset, publish_page · Destructive: run_cro_skill, get_audit, generate_concepts, fetch.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_cro_skills, run_cro_skill, get_audit_report, get_concepts, get_build, search, get_asset, publish_page · Private data: build_page, get_build, share_page, get_asset, publish_page, save_note, get_notes · Public sink: share_page, export_page, get_asset, publish_page · Destructive: run_cro_skill, get_audit, generate_concepts, fetch

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "run_cro_skill" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
